## TITLE
Wearable Turn Signal Band

## BACKGROUND
Cyclists signal turns with hand gestures that drivers often miss at night.

## SUMMARY
A wearable signaling device includes a flexible band, a light emitter mounted on the band, a motion sensor, and a controller. The controller activates the light emitter when the motion sensor detects a hand gesture.

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
FIG. 1 is a perspective view of the band. FIG. 2 is an exploded view. FIG. 3 is a flowchart of gesture classification.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION
The flexible band 20 may be an elastic strap or an adjustable strap with a hook-and-loop closure. A light emitter 30, such as an LED array, is mounted on the band 20. A battery 32 is housed in the band. A housing 34 encloses the controller 36 and may be rigid or semi-rigid.

A motion sensor 38, such as a three-axis accelerometer, detects a hand gesture. A signal processing module 37 in the controller classifies the motion and distinguishes a left-turn gesture from a right-turn gesture. The controller selects a blink pattern based on a direction of the hand gesture, for example a sweeping amber arrow that points in the direction of the turn.

A dampening member 40 sits between the band 20 and the light emitter 30. The controller reads the sensor at a sampling rate of at least 50 Hz and flashes the light emitter at a rate of 2 Hz. A haptic motor 42 vibrates to confirm the hand gesture. The device may transmit a signal to a helmet. A charging dock with an inductive coil and a status light recharges the battery.

## ABSTRACT
A wearable band with a light emitter that a controller activates when a motion sensor detects a hand-signal gesture.
